text: Should a people accustomed to live under a prince by any accident become free... a people in such circumstances may be likened to the wild animal which, though destined by nature to roam at large in the woods, has been reared in the cage and in constant confinement and which, should it chance to be set free in the open country, being unused to find its own food, and unfamiliar with the coverts where it might lie concealed, falls a prey to the first who seeks to recapture it.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
reference: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
